@package unison-util-rope
@version 0.0.0


-- | A strict finger tree.
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>amortized O(1) <a>cons</a>, <a>snoc</a>, <a>uncons</a>,
--   <a>unsnoc</a> when a sequence is used once; O(log n) in the worst
--   case, which a program can hit repeatedly only by going back to the
--   same old version</li>
--   <li>O(1) <a>size</a></li>
--   <li>O(log n) <a>lookup</a>, <a>append</a>, <a>take</a>,
--   <a>drop</a></li>
--   <li>no laziness anywhere: every field is strict, nothing is a
--   thunk</li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   The shape is Hinze and Paterson's: a prefix digit, a middle that is a
--   sequence of nodes, a suffix digit. The differences are that the middle
--   is strict, digits hold up to <a>maxD</a> items, and nodes are mostly
--   eight wide. The one invariant is that both digits of a tree with a
--   middle have an item (so the ends, and what is near them, are found
--   without going down). A digit that fills up sheds a node of eight into
--   the middle, and a digit that empties takes a node out of it.
--   
--   Digits are short lists, so that adding or removing an item at an end
--   allocates one cell or none. A node's children are in an array (or, for
--   the nodes of eight leaves, in the node itself): a node is built once
--   and then only read.
module Unison.Util.Deque.Internal
type Seq = Deque
pattern Empty :: Deque a
pattern (:<|) :: a -> Deque a -> Deque a
infixr 5 :<|
pattern (:|>) :: Deque a -> a -> Deque a
infixl 5 :|>
empty :: Deque a
singleton :: a -> Deque a
cons :: a -> Deque a -> Deque a
snoc :: Deque a -> a -> Deque a
append :: Deque a -> Deque a -> Deque a
(<|) :: a -> Deque a -> Deque a
infixr 5 <|
(|>) :: Deque a -> a -> Deque a
infixl 5 |>
(><) :: Deque a -> Deque a -> Deque a
infixr 5 ><

-- | O(n). A fold, so that it fuses with a list that is being produced.
fromList :: [a] -> Deque a

-- | <a>fromList</a> for a list whose length is known. O(n). Exactly
--   <tt>n</tt> elements are taken; a shorter list is an error.
--   (<a>unsafeFromListN</a> is the same without the check, for a caller
--   that built the list to length.)
fromListN :: Int -> [a] -> Deque a

-- | <a>fromListN</a> for a list known to have exactly <tt>n</tt> elements.
--   O(n). Builds the levels directly: each gets a prefix of two to nine
--   items and a suffix of five, and what is between them goes, in nodes of
--   eight, to the level below. The count is trusted: with more elements
--   than <tt>n</tt> the suffix holds them all while the packed count says
--   five, and a later append writes outside an array.
unsafeFromListN :: Int -> [a] -> Deque a

-- | <tt>fromFunction n f</tt> is <tt>f 0, f 1, ..., f (n - 1)</tt>.
fromFunction :: Int -> (Int -> a) -> Deque a
size :: Deque a -> Int
length :: Deque a -> Int
null :: Deque a -> Bool
lookup :: Int -> Deque a -> Maybe a

-- | The elements in order. Lazy: the list is produced as it is consumed.
toList :: Deque a -> [a]
uncons :: Deque a -> Maybe (a, Deque a)
unsnoc :: Deque a -> Maybe (Deque a, a)
take :: Int -> Deque a -> Deque a
drop :: Int -> Deque a -> Deque a

-- | <pre>
--   splitAt i d = (take i d, drop i d)
--   </pre>
splitAt :: Int -> Deque a -> (Deque a, Deque a)

-- | A stable sort. O(n log n); goes through a list.
sort :: Ord a => Deque a -> Deque a
sortBy :: (a -> a -> Ordering) -> Deque a -> Deque a

-- | The same as <a>sort</a> here; Data.Sequence has both.
unstableSort :: Ord a => Deque a -> Deque a
unstableSortBy :: (a -> a -> Ordering) -> Deque a -> Deque a
intersperse :: a -> Deque a -> Deque a
reverse :: Deque a -> Deque a
valid :: Deque a -> Either String ()
data Deque a
Nil :: Deque a
Deep :: !Int -> !SList a -> !Mid a -> !SList a -> Deque a
data SList a
SNil :: SList a
SCons :: !a -> !SList a -> SList a
data Node a
N8 :: !a -> !a -> !a -> !a -> !a -> !a -> !a -> !a -> Node a
NA :: !Int -> !Arr a -> Node a
data Mid a
MNil :: Mid a
MDeep :: !Int -> !Int -> !SList (Node a) -> !Mid (Node a) -> !SList (Node a) -> Mid a
type Arr = SmallArray
takeS :: Int -> SList a -> SList a
dropS :: Int -> SList a -> SList a
appendS :: SList a -> SList a -> SList a
lenS :: SList a -> Int
revS :: SList a -> SList a
revOnto :: SList a -> SList a -> SList a
listS :: SList a -> [a]
arr8 :: a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> Arr a
fromSListA :: Int -> SList a -> Arr a
nodeSize :: Node a -> Int
nodeArity :: Node a -> Int
nodeAt :: Int -> Node a -> a
nodeTakeRev :: Int -> Node a -> SList a
nodeDropFwd :: Int -> Node a -> SList a
maxD :: Int
mk :: Int -> Int -> Int -> Int
tsize :: Int -> Int
tpc :: Int -> Int
tsc :: Int -> Int
sizeM :: Mid a -> Int
consM :: Node a -> Mid a -> Mid a
snocM :: Mid a -> Node a -> Mid a
unconsM :: Mid a -> (Node a, Mid a)
unsnocM :: Mid a -> (Mid a, Node a)
scanFwd :: Int -> SList (Node a) -> (Node a, Int)
scanBwd :: Int -> SList (Node a) -> (Node a, Int)
scanKids :: Int -> Node (Node a) -> (Int, Int)
takeM :: Int -> Mid a -> (Mid a, Node a, Int)
dropM :: Int -> Mid a -> (Node a, Int, Mid a)
appM :: Mid a -> Int -> SList (Node a) -> Mid a -> Mid a
foldrM :: (Node a -> r -> r) -> r -> Mid a -> r

foldrNode :: (a -> r -> r) -> Node a -> r -> r
foldlM :: (r -> Node a -> r) -> r -> Mid a -> r
foldlS :: (r -> a -> r) -> r -> SList a -> r
foldlRev :: (r -> a -> r) -> r -> SList a -> r
foldlNode :: (r -> a -> r) -> r -> Node a -> r
validM :: Int -> (a -> Either String Int) -> Mid a -> Either String Int
instance Data.Functor.Classes.Eq1 Unison.Util.Deque.Internal.Deque
instance GHC.Classes.Eq a => GHC.Classes.Eq (Unison.Util.Deque.Internal.Deque a)
instance GHC.Internal.Data.Foldable.Foldable Unison.Util.Deque.Internal.Deque
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Functor Unison.Util.Deque.Internal.Deque
instance GHC.Internal.IsList.IsList (Unison.Util.Deque.Internal.Deque a)
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Monoid (Unison.Util.Deque.Internal.Deque a)
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData a => Control.DeepSeq.NFData (Unison.Util.Deque.Internal.Deque a)
instance Data.Functor.Classes.Ord1 Unison.Util.Deque.Internal.Deque
instance GHC.Classes.Ord a => GHC.Classes.Ord (Unison.Util.Deque.Internal.Deque a)
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Semigroup (Unison.Util.Deque.Internal.Deque a)
instance Data.Functor.Classes.Show1 Unison.Util.Deque.Internal.Deque
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show a => GHC.Internal.Show.Show (Unison.Util.Deque.Internal.Deque a)

-- | A strict finger tree: see <a>Unison.Util.Deque.Internal</a>, which has

-- | A rope: a sequence of chunks that knows its size in elements (the
--   characters of a text, the bytes of a byte string).
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>O(1) <a>size</a></li>
--   <li>amortized O(1) <a>cons</a>, <a>snoc</a>, <a>uncons</a>,
--   <a>unsnoc</a> of a chunk, and so of a short piece of text at either
--   end</li>
--   <li>O(log n) <a>index</a>, <a>take</a>, <a>drop</a>, append; close to
--   O(1) near either end</li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   It is the finger tree of <a>Unison.Util.Deque</a> with chunks for
--   elements and sizes counted in what the chunks hold. The middle of the
--   tree is the Deque's own middle, a sequence of nodes that knows the
--   size under each; only the top level, whose items are chunks, is
--   written here.
--   
--   Invariants:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>no chunk is empty</li>
--   <li>a rope of one chunk is <a>One</a>; a <a>Deep</a> has a chunk in
--   each digit</li>
--   <li>two chunks next to each other hold more than <a>threshold</a>
--   elements between them, so a rope of n elements has at most <tt>2n /
--   threshold + 1</tt> chunks however it was built</li>
--   </ul>
module Unison.Util.Rope
chunks :: Rope a -> [a]
fromChunks :: (Sized a, Semigroup a) => [a] -> Rope a
singleton :: Sized a => a -> Rope a
one :: Sized a => a -> Rope a

-- | The result is rebuilt from the chunks the function returns, so it is a
--   rope whatever their sizes are.
map :: (Sized b, Semigroup b) => (a -> b) -> Rope a -> Rope b
traverse :: (Applicative f, Sized b, Semigroup b) => (a -> f b) -> Rope a -> f (Rope b)
traverseWithPos_ :: (Applicative f, Sized a) => (Int -> a -> f ()) -> Rope a -> f ()
null :: Rope a -> Bool
flatten :: Monoid a => Rope a -> a
two :: (Sized a, Semigroup a) => Rope a -> Rope a -> Rope a
cons :: (Sized a, Semigroup a) => a -> Rope a -> Rope a
uncons :: Sized a => Rope a -> Maybe (a, Rope a)
snoc :: (Sized a, Semigroup a) => Rope a -> a -> Rope a
unsnoc :: Sized a => Rope a -> Maybe (Rope a, a)
index :: (Sized a, Index a ch) => Int -> Rope a -> Maybe ch

-- | The number of levels below the top one.
debugDepth :: Rope a -> Int
extractChunk :: (Monoid a, Sized a, Take a, Drop a) => Int -> Int -> Rope a -> a

-- | Two chunks next to each other with this many elements or fewer between
--   them are made one chunk.
--   
--   See
--   <a>https://github.com/unisonweb/unison/pull/1899#discussion_r742953469</a>
threshold :: Int

-- | Checks the invariants.
valid :: Sized a => Rope a -> Either String ()
class Sized a
size :: Sized a => a -> Int
class Take a
take :: Take a => Int -> a -> a
class Drop a
drop :: Drop a => Int -> a -> a
class Reverse a
reverse :: Reverse a => a -> a
class Index a elem
unsafeIndex :: Index a elem => Int -> a -> elem

-- | The first <a>Int</a> of <a>Deep</a> packs three numbers, as in the
--   Deque: the size of the rope (bits 8 and up), the number of chunks in
--   the suffix (bits 4 to 7) and in the prefix (bits 0 to 3). The second
--   is the size of the prefix. The prefix runs front to back and the
--   suffix back to front, so the first and last chunks of the rope are the
--   heads of the two lists.
data Rope a
Empty :: Rope a
One :: !a -> Rope a
Deep :: !Int -> !Int -> !SList a -> !Mid a -> !SList a -> Rope a
instance (Unison.Util.Rope.Sized a, GHC.Internal.Base.Semigroup a, Unison.Util.Rope.Drop a) => Unison.Util.Rope.Drop (Unison.Util.Rope.Rope a)
instance (Unison.Util.Rope.Sized a, Unison.Util.Rope.Take a, Unison.Util.Rope.Drop a, GHC.Classes.Eq a) => GHC.Classes.Eq (Unison.Util.Rope.Rope a)
instance GHC.Internal.Data.Foldable.Foldable Unison.Util.Rope.Rope
instance (Unison.Util.Rope.Sized a, Unison.Util.Rope.Index a ch) => Unison.Util.Rope.Index (Unison.Util.Rope.Rope a) ch
instance (Unison.Util.Rope.Sized a, GHC.Internal.Base.Semigroup a) => GHC.Internal.Base.Monoid (Unison.Util.Rope.Rope a)
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData a => Control.DeepSeq.NFData (Unison.Util.Rope.Rope a)
instance (Unison.Util.Rope.Sized a, Unison.Util.Rope.Take a, Unison.Util.Rope.Drop a, GHC.Classes.Ord a) => GHC.Classes.Ord (Unison.Util.Rope.Rope a)
instance (Unison.Util.Rope.Sized a, GHC.Internal.Base.Semigroup a, Unison.Util.Rope.Reverse a) => Unison.Util.Rope.Reverse (Unison.Util.Rope.Rope a)
instance (Unison.Util.Rope.Sized a, GHC.Internal.Base.Semigroup a) => GHC.Internal.Base.Semigroup (Unison.Util.Rope.Rope a)
instance Unison.Util.Rope.Sized a => Unison.Util.Rope.Sized (Unison.Util.Rope.Rope a)
instance (Unison.Util.Rope.Sized a, GHC.Internal.Base.Semigroup a, Unison.Util.Rope.Take a) => Unison.Util.Rope.Take (Unison.Util.Rope.Rope a)
